commitments.text: Cooling Water Blowdown: A continuous or periodic purge of cooling water will be required in order to prevent the build up of contaminants. This blowdown stream will be connected into the Mill wastewater collection and treatment system.

Stormwater: Open drains will be used to collect stormwater from the developed area of the site, including runoff from truck unloading, equipment, roofs and other process areas. Sediment and grease traps will be used as appropriate, and curbs will be provided around pumps, oil tanks and other relevant equipment to contain spills and also prevent stormwater from entering the drain in the curbed area. Where location and finished grade of the terrain permit, drainage from the plant site will be designed to flow to Casey Creek. All other stormwater flows (including that from all process areas) will discharge to the Mill stormwater drainage and treatment system. Stormwater runoff from the access road will flow to shallow ditches, culverts and natural drainage channels to Casey Creek.

Demineralization Waste: Wastewater will be produced during the regeneration of ion exchange resins in the water demineralization columns. This wastewater will be neutralized and discharged to the Mill wastewater collection and treatment system.

Process Area Drains: For areas where potentially hazardous materials are stored or used (such as transformer bays and oil storage tanks), oil interception facilities and other mechanisms will be designed and installed to ensure that all spills are contained. Provisions will also be included to segregate and remove oily waste thereby allowing clean wastewater to pass directly to the Mill. All floor and equipment drains will be monitored for oily waste and provision will be made to retain the discharge for cleanup prior to discharging to the Mill's wastewater treatment facilities. Material storage areas will be provided with stormwater drain valves (normally closed) so as to contain spills and leaks.
Sanitary Wastes: Wastewater from domestic water use will be routed to the sanitary waste collection and treatment system at the Mill.

Noise Control: All applicable noise regulations will be met, including relevant parts of the Workers' Compensation Act of British Columbia and the Industrial Health and Safety Regulations. In addition to meeting the above regulations, the ICP facility will not exceed noise levels as set out in Table 3.1-6 (Maximum Facility Noise Levels).

Maximum facility noise level of 85 dBA at 1 m from all equipment (under calm, clear and stable atmospheric conditions with the Elk Falls Mill operating at a similar condition to that during the noise baseline survey). Based on a review of typical industrial construction methods used during the construction phase, a guideline was provided to the turnkey bidders which sets out means to mitigate the noise impact on the community during the construction period.

All contractor equipment used on-site shall be fitted with intake and exhaust mufflers meeting the manufacturer's recommendations for sound attenuation consistent with operational limitations. ICP reserves the right to have non-compliant equipment removed from the site.
Pile driving hours shall be maintained between the hours of 0800h and 1900h during the normal work week of Monday through Friday.
Pile driving outside the 0800h-1900h weekday hours is not permitted unless specifically approved by the parties having jurisdiction and ICP.
Local municipality by-laws mandate that 2200h to 0700h are quiet hours. Any work performed during this period shall generate no appreciable noise and must have the approval of the ICP representative.

Waste generated by ICP will be managed to ensure all applicable regulations are met. In conformance with the Comox-Strathcona Regional District waste management plan, waste will be minimized at source and will be recycled to the extent practical.

During construction, the primary access route would be used for construction traffic with the exception of very heavy trucks which would use the main Mill road. ICP will also make reasonable efforts to make maximum use of barge transport where feasible. Mitigation of any background noise impacts will be achieved through the use of berms beside the new access road. In addition, construction traffic will be controlled and monitored to mitigate noise impacts to the local neighbourhood.

The Island Cogeneration Project will control NOx emissions through the use of dry low NOx combustion technology which will control emissions to 25 ppm while burning natural gas. During the times of liquid fuel firing, water injection will be utilized to control NOx, which is currently the best technology available from suppliers of advanced large gas turbines.

Waste will be generated at the proposed Island Cogeneration plant from process operations, maintenance work, and during plant construction. In conformance with the Comox-Strathcona Regional District Waste Management Plan strategy, waste generation will be minimized and recycling will be carried out where practical. During plant construction, generated wastes will be minimized, reused and recycled if feasible; recyclable metals, cardboard and plastics will be separated at source and transported off-site for recycling.

No person shall create a nuisance to any person who contends their interest in property is affected, including the surrounding residents and general public, by reason of unsightliness, odour emission, dust, noise, smoke, or electrical interference.
